correctness.rationale: For \(e=rs+t\), Frobenius induction gives the surviving corner \(P^{p^e-p^t}\) at power \(\lfloor(p^e-1)/(q-1)\rfloor\); multiplying by the germ kills it. For the Fermat sum, the \(p^s\)-th power vanishes and a Lucas-nonzero mixed term survives at power \(p^s-1\). The smooth leading Fermat form and initial Jacobian regular sequence give multiplicity \(q+1\) and Milnor length \(q^n\). Exact sparse-polynomial computations corroborate the stated finite parameter tests.

value.rationale: Responds to the natural question raised by Svoray perturbation examples: do a smooth fixed projective tangent cone and a fixed Milnor number force identical F-pure thresholds? The answer is no, with an exact all-prime/all-dimension one-parameter family and a uniform positive jump. The Frobenius-corner rigidity theorem determines all Frobenius exponents and identifies a broad ideal-theoretic mechanism rather than an arbitrary low-dimensional numerical slice.
